{{Short description|Endless sequence of integers}}

In [[mathematics]] and [[computer science]], '''Recamán's sequence'''<ref name="oeis">{{Cite OEIS|A005132|Recamán's sequence}}</ref><ref name="MathWorld">{{MathWorld|id=RecamansSequence|title=Recamán's Sequence}}</ref> is a [[sequence]] defined by a [[recurrence relation]]. Because its elements are related to the previous elements in a straightforward way, they are often defined using [[Recursive definition|recursion]].

[[File:Recamán_Sequence_Visualisation.svg|thumb|250px|right|A drawing of the first 75 terms of Recamán's sequence, according to the method of visualization shown in the [[Numberphile]] video "The Slightly Spooky Recamán Sequence"<ref name="numberphile">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FGC5TdIiT9U The Slightly Spooky Recamán Sequence], Numberphile video.</ref>]]

Recamán's sequence was named after its inventor, Colombian mathematician {{ill|Bernardo Recamán Santos|es}}, by [[Neil Sloane]], creator of the [[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]] (OEIS).
__TOC__

== Definition ==
Recamán's sequence <math>a_0, a_1, a_2\dots</math> is defined as:

: <math>a_n = \begin{cases}
0 && \text{if } n = 0 \\
a_{n - 1} -n && \text{if } a_{n - 1} -n > 0 \text{ and is not already in the sequence} \\
a_{n - 1} + n && \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}</math>

The first terms of the sequence are:
:0, 1, 3, 6, 2, 7, 13, 20, 12, 21, 11, 22, 10, 23, 9, 24, 8, 25, 43, 62, 42, 63, 41, 18, 42, 17, 43, 16, 44, 15, 45, 14, 46, 79, 113, 78, 114, 77, 39, 78, 38, 79, 37, 80, 36, 81, 35, 82, 34, 83, 33, 84, 32, 85, 31, 86, 30, 87, 29, 88, 28, 89, 27, 90, 26, 91, 157, 224, 156, 225, 155, ... {{OEIS|id=A005132}}

== Sound representation ==
{{Listen|title="Recamán's sequence"|filename=recaman.mid|description="Play Recamán's sequence."|help=no}}

Values of the sequence can be associated with musical notes, in such that the running of the sequence can be associated with an execution of a musical tune.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://oeis.org/play?seq=A005132 |title=Play a Sequence |website=The [[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]]}}</ref>

== Properties ==
The sequence satisfies:

: <math>a_n \geq 0</math>
: <math>|a_n - a_{n-1}| = n</math>
While the sequence attempts to avoid repeated terms while subtracting, it does not do so while adding, and repeats do in fact occur. Since there are repeated terms, this is not a permutation of the integers.

The first repeated term is <math>42 = a_{24} = a_{20}</math>.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://mathlesstraveled.com/2016/06/12/the-recaman-sequence/ |title=Math less traveled |access-date=2019-12-14 |archive-date=2023-07-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230711110214/https://mathlesstraveled.com/2016/06/12/the-recaman-sequence/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> Another one is <math>43 = a_{18} = a_{26}</math>.

=== Conjecture ===
[[Neil Sloane]] has conjectured that every number eventually appears, but this has not been proven. As of 2026, {{val|e=612}} terms have been calculated, and 852,655 is the smallest natural number to not appear on the list.
